errorCodes.meaning: The `purpose` is not one this service implements. This version defines `login` only.
The `mode` is not one this service implements. This version defines `scan` only.
The document's issuer is not an Ed25519 `did:key`.
The starter's network has hit the service's limit on requests or on pending requests. `details.retryAfter` MAY give seconds until a retry.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Mode.description: How the request reaches the approver. A CLOSED list. Version 0.1 defines `scan`: the starter shows a trigger link (as a QR code that is also a clickable link, TRIGGER-LINK.md) and the approver's wallet reads it. `code` (a typed code of at least 8 characters, under strict rate limits) and `push` (sent to the approver's enrolled devices) are reserved names.
Mode.title: Mode

Purpose.description: What the request is for. A CLOSED list: each purpose has a fixed row in CONVENTIONS.md §3 stating what is revealed at each step, what the grant contains, what redeem returns and the window lengths. Version 0.1 defines `login` only. `stepUp` and `deviceEnrol` are reserved names; adding one is a new version of this component and of every task that references it, never an in-place edit.
Purpose.title: Purpose

RequestId.description: The service-generated handle of one request: 16 to 32 bytes from a cryptographically secure random source, written as unpadded base64url (22 to 43 characters; 16 bytes, 22 characters, is RECOMMENDED). It is also the nonce of the exchange, so the family needs no separate challenge, and it is the `_id` of the trigger link (VTI-LNK-033). Compared as a string. It confers no authority on its holder.
RequestId.title: RequestId

Response.description: The handle of the new request and the instant its claim window closes. The starter builds the trigger link from these and the service's DID.

claimClosesAt.description: The instant by which the request must be claimed, as an RFC 3339 date-time. The trigger link's `_exp` carries the same instant in the link's own integer form: the starter converts this value into it when it builds the link. At most 180 s after the request was accepted; 120 s is RECOMMENDED.

schema.description: A starter asks a service to open an out-of-band request that an approver will decide on another device. The document is issued and signed by the starter's fresh Ed25519 key, which is fixed for the life of the request. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.
